facts.text: Road-car automatic braking assumes a well-characterized tire-road interface.
facts.quote: Road-car automatic braking assumes a well-characterized tire-road interface.

facts.text: Earth-moving machines routinely operate on loose aggregate, mud, soft soil, snow, wet clay and deep material, where the ground interface changes shear capacity, sinkage, rolling resistance, slip and directional response.
facts.quote: loose aggregate, mud, soft soil, snow, wet clay and deep material change shear capacity, sinkage, rolling resistance, slip and directional response.

facts.text: Bekker and Wong terramechanics, summarized in a US Army report, shows that tractive and braking force depend on soil type, contact area, load and slip.
facts.quote: Bekker and Wong terramechanics, summarized in a US Army report, shows that tractive and braking force depend on soil type, contact area, load and slip

facts.text: Bekker and Wong terramechanics, summarized in a US Army report, shows that tracks keep more shear force than tires in soft soil.
facts.quote: tracks keep more shear force than tires in soft soil.

facts.text: A 2023 Journal of Terramechanics model covering all slip and skid states, with slip ratio −1 to 0.9 and slip angle 0° to 60°, predicted forces well in sand.
facts.quote: A 2023 Journal of Terramechanics model covering all slip and skid states (slip ratio −1 to 0.9, slip angle 0° to 60°) predicted forces well in sand

facts.text: Some tuning parameters in the 2023 Journal of Terramechanics model depend on slip angle, so the parameters do not transfer cleanly between conditions.
facts.quote: "a dependence of some tuning parameters on slip angle is observed", so the parameters do not transfer cleanly between conditions.

facts.text: A 2026 terrain-deformation model shows soil building up in front of the wheel during braking.
facts.quote: A 2026 terrain-deformation model shows soil building up in front of the wheel during braking

facts.text: A 2026 terrain-deformation model shows drawbar pull growing more negative as slip becomes more negative during braking.
facts.quote: with drawbar pull growing more negative as slip becomes more negative.

facts.text: The cited terramechanics and terrain-deformation findings were tested on single-wheel rigs and sand, not full machines.
facts.quote: All of this was tested on single-wheel rigs and sand, not full machines.

facts.text: Open-source and commercial frameworks expose deformable-terrain models to address ground-interface dynamics.
facts.quote: Open-source and commercial frameworks expose deformable-terrain models for this reason.

facts.text: Project Chrono supports rigid terrain, the semi-empirical Soil Contact Model with Bekker-Wong pressure-sinkage and shear parameters, and more expensive granular or deformable approaches.
facts.quote: Project Chrono supports rigid terrain, the semi-empirical Soil Contact Model (Bekker-Wong pressure-sinkage and shear parameters) and more expensive granular or deformable approaches

facts.text: Altair's tracked-vehicle workflow models tracked machines over soft soil and can couple multibody simulation to granular EDEM models.
facts.quote: Altair's tracked-vehicle workflow models tracked machines over soft soil and can couple multibody simulation to granular EDEM models.

facts.text: The documented terrain-model capabilities of Project Chrono and Altair do not prove that either predicts a specific machine's emergency stopping distance to a stated error.
facts.quote: These are tool capabilities, not proof that either predicts a specific machine's emergency stopping distance to a stated error.

facts.text: A generally applicable table of friction values for wet dirt, gravel or mud reliable enough to set automatic-braking thresholds across the earth-moving-machine product range was not found.
facts.quote: A generally applicable table of friction values for wet dirt, gravel or mud reliable enough to set automatic-braking thresholds across this product range: not found.

facts.text: Published full-machine braking distance on wet clay or loose gravel was not found.
facts.quote: Published full-machine braking distance on wet clay or loose gravel: not found.

facts.text: Effective braking capability for earth-moving machines has to be measured or estimated as a machine, terrain and state distribution rather than selected from a handbook coefficient.
facts.quote: Effective braking capability therefore has to be measured or estimated as a machine, terrain and state distribution rather than selected from a handbook coefficient.
